headline: DSE: Three companies dropped from DS30 blue-chip index
summary: Linde Bangladesh, Kohinoor Chemicals, and Unique Hotel & Resorts are out, while three others enter as part of the semi-annual rebalancing.
details: The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) has removed Linde Bangladesh, Kohinoor Chemicals, and Unique Hotel & Resorts from its blue-chip index, DS30, effective July 19.
In their place, Bangladesh Steel Re-Rolling Mills, The ACME Laboratories, and Power Grid Company of Bangladesh have been added to the index.
The DS30 serves as the investable benchmark for the DSE, tracking the performance of 30 of the most liquid and fundamentally strong blue-chip companies.
Designed in partnership with S&P Dow Jones Indices, the index is rebalanced twice a year, typically in January and July.
To qualify for inclusion, a company must have a float-adjusted market capitalisation above Tk 50 crore and a minimum three-month average daily traded value of Tk 50 lakh.
Additionally, companies must be fundamentally profitable, showing positive net income over the latest 12-month period as of the rebalancing date.
Mutual funds, debentures, and corporate or government bonds are excluded from the index regardless of their size.
caption:
Three major companies just lost their spot in the DSE's blue-chip index. Who's in and who's out?

The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) has removed Linde Bangladesh, Kohinoor Chemicals, and Unique Hotel & Resorts from its blue-chip index, DS30, effective July 19.

In their place, Bangladesh Steel Re-Rolling Mills, The ACME Laboratories, and Power Grid Company of Bangladesh have been added to the index.

The DS30 serves as the investable benchmark for the DSE, tracking the performance of 30 of the most liquid and fundamentally strong blue-chip companies.

Designed in partnership with S&P Dow Jones Indices, the index is rebalanced twice a year, typically in January and July.

To qualify for inclusion, a company must have a float-adjusted market capitalisation above Tk 50 crore and a minimum three-month average daily traded value of Tk 50 lakh.

Additionally, companies must be fundamentally profitable, showing positive net income over the latest 12-month period as of the rebalancing date.

Mutual funds, debentures, and corporate or government bonds are excluded from the index regardless of their size.

headline_marked: Heavy rain: [[DU postpones all internal exams]] for Monday
headline: Heavy rain: DU postpones all internal exams for Monday
summary: Severe waterlogging at student halls and across the capital has forced Dhaka University to reschedule Monday's tests.
details: Dhaka University has postponed all internal examinations scheduled for Monday, July 13, due to severe weather conditions and widespread waterlogging.
The decision was announced in a press release from the university's controller of examinations office on Sunday night.
Heavy rainfall led to significant waterlogging in several areas of the campus, particularly affecting the Bangamata Sheikh Fazyilatunnessa Mujib Hall and the Bangladesh-Kuwait Friendship Hall.
Following appeals from students facing these difficulties, the university administration decided to suspend the exams to ensure student safety and accessibility.
New schedules for the postponed exams will be announced in due course, based on proposals from the respective departments or institutes.
However, the university clarified that examinations at affiliated and constituent colleges and institutes will proceed as per the original schedule.
The weather-induced disruption comes amid broader reports of severe waterlogging across Dhaka city, affecting daily commutes and public life.
caption:
Heavy rain and campus flooding force Dhaka University to cancel Monday's exams.

Dhaka University has postponed all internal examinations scheduled for Monday, July 13, due to severe weather conditions and widespread waterlogging.

The decision was announced in a press release from the university's controller of examinations office on Sunday night.

Heavy rainfall led to significant waterlogging in several areas of the campus, particularly affecting the Bangamata Sheikh Fazyilatunnessa Mujib Hall and the Bangladesh-Kuwait Friendship Hall.

Following appeals from students facing these difficulties, the university administration decided to suspend the exams to ensure student safety and accessibility.

New schedules for the postponed exams will be announced in due course, based on proposals from the respective departments or institutes.

However, the university clarified that examinations at affiliated and constituent colleges and institutes will proceed as per the original schedule.

The weather-induced disruption comes amid broader reports of severe waterlogging across Dhaka city, affecting daily commutes and public life.
